title: The AI-Powered Fixed Income Trader: Navigating the Future of Market Intelligence
summary: I started my career on a corporate credit trading desk, and back then, market intelligence was something you built by hand, calling multiple counterparties, manually pulling data from a half-dozen systems and reading through stacks of research to piece together a view of where a bond should trade. Just as importantly, you built trusted relationships. The conversations you had with clients and counterparties provided context that data alone couldn't, and those relationships were often as valuable as the information itself.
body_text: I started my career on a corporate credit trading desk, and back then, market intelligence was something you built by hand, calling multiple counterparties, manually pulling data from a half-dozen systems and reading through stacks of research to piece together a view of where a bond should trade. Just as importantly, you built trusted relationships. The conversations you had with clients and counterparties provided context that data alone couldn't, and those relationships were often as valuable as the information itself. Today, that process looks completely different. What once required hours of manual effort can now be accomplished with a simple natural-language query, generating tailored insights on liquidity, pricing, historical execution performance, market activity and trade history. AI is making market intelligence faster, richer and more accessible than ever before. But while technology is transforming how traders access information, it isn't replacing the human relationships that underpin successful markets. If anything, by reducing the time spent gathering data, AI gives traders more opportunity to focus on the tasks and conversations that create lasting value. I’ve also seen this evolution firsthand at Tradeweb. Not long ago, clients would routinely reach out to our teams with questions that required us to manually pull together data and research. Today, AI is helping shift that approach from answering one question at a time to enabling clients to self-serve accurate, real-time market intelligence. That not only improves our own efficiency, but, more importantly, gives clients faster access to deeper insights, while allowing our teams to spend more time on higher-value conversations, helping clients navigate markets and solve complex problems. The recent launch of TARA ( Tradeweb AI Research Assistant ), Tradeweb’s AI-powered research assistant for institutional credit traders, is a powerful example of how far the industry has come and how AI is transforming the way traders can access and analyze market intelligence. By combining natural language capabilities with Tradeweb's proprietary market data and liquidity analytics, TARA enables traders to access insights in seconds that previously required many time-consuming, manual steps and multiple screens. The goal isn’t to replace the expertise or relationships that define successful trading, but to equip market participants with better information so they can make more informed decisions and have more meaningful conversations with clients and counterparties. Why fixed income is especially well positioned Fixed income markets are particularly well-suited to benefit from AI. Unlike equities, where centralized exchanges and continuous pricing create natural transparency, most fixed income instruments trade over-the-counter, across a fragmented web of dealers, platforms, protocols and workflows. Price discovery is complex. Liquidity is dispersed, and the sheer volume of bonds outstanding, along with bespoke derivatives, makes it nearly impossible for any single participant to maintain a complete picture of the market. The rise of electronic trading has dramatically increased market transparency and liquidity. But converting that wealth of information into timely, actionable insights remains challenging. AI can help bridge that gap. By combining proprietary market data, analytics and natural language interfaces, traders can interact with information in a far more intuitive way. Instead of searching through dashboards, reports and spreadsheets, they can ask questions and receive context-driven answers. That represents a meaningful shift in productivity, how investment decisions are made and the speed at which trading evolves. You start shifting the conversation from “where is this bond?” to “what’s the smartest way to execute this trade given everything happening in the market right now?” That’s a fundamentally different value proposition, and one that matters most in exactly the kind of complex, opaque markets where fixed income lives. The future isn’t just faster answers Today, AI, alongside electronic trading, is helping traders access information faster and more efficiently. Tomorrow, it may proactively surface insights before they're even requested, identify emerging market trends, automate workflows and deliver increasingly personalized intelligence based on a trader’s objectives and activity. While AI adoption in fixed income is still in its early stages, the trajectory is clear. Human expertise and relationships will remain essential, while trust, transparency and explainability will be critical as AI becomes increasingly embedded in trading workflows. Building the markets of the future with clients The firms that will define the next era of trading technology won’t be the ones building AI in isolation. They’ll be the ones building it in deep partnership with the clients and market participants who use it every day. At Tradeweb, that collaborative approach is core to how we operate. We don’t develop solutions and hand them to the market. We sit with traders, portfolio managers and dealers to understand how they work, where the friction is and what would genuinely help their process. TARA was built based on these conversations -- informed by real client workflows, refined through direct feedback and designed to solve problems that traders face every day. That same client-led approach will continue to shape how we develop AI capabilities across our platform as the technology evolves. The AI road ahead: from assistants to agents AI's impact will be felt across every stage of the trade lifecycle. It will transform how liquidity is sourced in illiquid markets, using pattern recognition to identify potential counterparties and optimal execution windows. It will reshape pre-trade analytics, synthesize macro signals, credit fundamentals and real-time market activity into unified views. And it will redefine post-trade intelligence, turning execution data into continuous feedback loops that sharpen future decisions. Human expertise remains essential. The judgment to override a model, the intuition that something doesn’t feel right, the relationships that underpin how markets function -- these aren’t going away. But the traders who combine that expertise with AI-powered intelligence will operate on a different level than those who don’t. The next generation of markets won't just be electronic. They'll be intelligent. At Tradeweb, we intend to help build that future by working alongside our clients to develop AI solutions that make markets more transparent, more efficient and more intuitive to navigate. The firms that succeed won’t just adopt AI – they’ll shape how it’s applied to real challenges traders face every day. That’s the role we see for ourselves: partnering with the market to build the next generation of intelligent trading.

title: Business case template for B2B sales
summary: A business case template for B2B sales you can copy: the five sections every buyer-ready case needs, a filled-in example, and how to generate it per deal.
body_text: Last updated: July 2026 A business case template for B2B sales is a reusable structure with five sections: the problem, the cost of inaction, the proposed solution, the ROI, and the recommendation. A rep personalizes each section per deal. The template below can be copied directly, or generated automatically from a blueprint so every rep starts from the same proven structure. This guide covers what a business case template is, the sections it should include, a template you can copy, a filled-in example, and how to run it once it is live. For a broader comparison of tools, see the best tools to create a business case for a sale. What is a business case template? A business case template is a standardized structure for the buyer-facing case that reps reuse across deals. It fixes the sections and default framing so each rep only fills in the account-specific details. A good template speeds up creation and keeps quality consistent across the whole sales team. Consistency is a real advantage. When every rep’s business case follows the same structure, finance knows where to find the ROI, the champion knows what to forward, and the sales leader can coach against one repeatable format. What should a business case template include? A business case template should include five sections in a deliberate order: the problem first, then the cost of inaction, the proposed solution, the ROI, and the recommendation. For the reasoning behind each, see what a sales business case should include. The problem: the specific pain in the buyer’s words. The cost of inaction: the quantified price of the status quo. The proposed solution: how the product solves it for this account. The ROI: the return, payback, and assumptions. The recommendation: a clear ask and next step. A business case template you can copy Copy the structure below and replace the bracketed prompts with account-specific content. Section 1: The problem [Buyer company] is facing [the specific problem in their words], which affects [the team or outcome at stake]. Section 2: The cost of inaction Staying with the status quo costs approximately [quantified impact: hours, revenue, risk, or missed growth] per [timeframe]. Section 3: The proposed solution [Product] solves this by [the two or three capabilities that matter for this deal], tied to the problem above. Section 4: The ROI Expected return: [figure]. Payback period: [timeframe]. Assumptions: [the key assumptions finance can check]. Section 5: The recommendation We recommend [the specific decision]. The next step is [the meeting, sign-off, or pilot] by [date]. For a complex deal, add a short appendix with a technical summary for IT, a security note for InfoSec, and the ROI detail for finance. The template, filled in Here is the same template completed for a hypothetical deal with Northstar, a 500-person SaaS company: Problem: Northstar’s RevOps team rebuilds the same pipeline reports by hand every week, which delays leadership’s forecast calls. Cost of inaction: about 10 hours a week of manual reporting, roughly $37,500 a year at a loaded $75 an hour. Solution: automate the reporting and surface live pipeline health, tied to the two workflows named in discovery. ROI: expected return about $37,500 a year in recovered time. Payback roughly six months on an $18,000 annual cost. Assumptions: 10 hours a week, $75 loaded rate. Recommendation: start a 30-day pilot on the two named workflows, with a go or no-go review at the end. Get the template as a ready-to-run blueprint The copy-and-fill version above is a fast start. To skip the fill-in step entirely, start from Mutiny’s pre-built business case blueprint: it holds the same five-section structure and generates the account-specific content for you, so the first draft is done in minutes. How to use the business case template Personalize every section for the deal, keep the core case to one or two pages, and share it where the buying group already works. Most buyers expect a business case: per Forrester, 97% of B2B buyers build one to justify a purchase. Lead with the problem and the cost of inaction, because Challenger found 40% to 60% of lost deals end in no decision, and the case has to beat the status quo before it beats a competitor. From static template to a generated business case A copy-and-fill template is a strong start, and the best sales teams take it further by generating each case automatically. A static template still leaves every rep to research the account, quantify the cost of inaction, and build the ROI by hand for each deal. Generating that content from the template turns hours of work into minutes and keeps the whole team consistent. How Mutiny turns the template into a personalized business case Mutiny is the top-rated AI tool for creating personalized deal content and GTM workflow automation. Mutiny starts from a pre-built business case blueprint and generates the personalized content itself: the problem, the cost of inaction, the ROI, and the recommendation for the specific account, in minutes. This runs as a two-sided model. The agent creates the case, and reps and marketers build their own agents and routines to automate the surrounding work, from follow-ups to keeping the numbers current. Sales leaders can standardize the blueprint so every rep runs the same play, and any AE can produce a deal-ready case on day one with no value team required. “With the template library, I can spin up personalized assets in minutes. Being able to give people what they need at the right moment, that’s a huge differentiator right now.” Kevin Jong, Principal GTM AI Operator, Genesis Computing

title: The Ultimate Guide to Restaurant Recruitment Marketing in 2025
summary: Discover how recruitment marketing helps restaurants cut turnover, save on hiring costs, and attract top talent.
body_text: The biggest threat to restaurant profitability isn’t food costs or a labor shortage. It’s turnover. Turnover is quietly crushing P&Ls across the industry — draining thousands in recruitment expenses, training costs, lost productivity, and operational chaos, and causing burnout to people operators and hiring teams. But here’s a secret: the problem isn’t a lack of workers looking for jobs. It’s about how you’re consistently and effectively attracting top talent. Most restaurants are still relying on outdated hiring methods that don’t work in today’s competitive labor market. Pouring thousands into job ad boosting? That just burns cash while unqualified candidates flood in. The solution? Recruitment marketing. Recruitment marketing is your secret weapon for consistently attracting top talent before your competitors do — and turning hiring from a cost center into a competitive advantage. Today, we’ll break down what recruitment marketing really looks like in restaurants and hospitality , and share 4 key takeaways to help you attract, engage, and convert top talent faster. What Do You Mean by Recruitment Marketing? Before we begin, let’s take a look at exactly what recruitment marketing is. Every successful restaurant knows how to market to customers. Iconic taglines, recognizable colors, memorable experiences—you understand what resonates with diners because it drives revenue. But while customer marketing answers "Why should I eat at your restaurant instead of the one down the street?", recruitment marketing answers "Why should I work at your restaurant instead of the one down the street?" Instead of waiting for applicants to find you, recruitment marketing proactively builds your employer brand, creates compelling candidate experiences, and nurtures talent relationships over time. In order to maximize your chances at attracting top hospitality talent, this means shifting from reactive "Help Wanted" signs to strategic campaigns that showcase your culture, career growth opportunities, and unique value proposition to potential employees. The Restaurant Recruitment Marketing Challenge in 2025 Why Traditional Recruiting Falls Short While restaurants have continually pushed the boundaries of food service and hospitality, recruitment marketing remains an overlooked piece of restaurant operations. The disconnect is costly: 76% of restaurant operators report difficulty finding qualified candidates, and time-to-fill for key positions now averages 28 days. The problem isn't lack of available talent—it's that most restaurant groups are still using recruitment strategies from a decade ago while competing for attention with brands that have embraced modern marketing principles. Most restaurant groups still rely on outdated approaches: Generic job postings that blend into the noise No clear employer brand differentiation Poor candidate communication and follow-up Limited use of social media and digital channels Lack of data-driven recruitment marketing frameworks The result? You're essentially running a marketing campaign with 1990s tactics while your competition—and candidates—have moved into the digital age. Effective Recruitment Marketing = Quality Hires That Stay A cutting edge recruitment marketing strategy isn’t just a good idea in concept – it’s been proven to drive serious results. Torchy’s Tacos, the viral Austin hotspot known for their Damn Good tacos and queso, leveraged advanced recruitment marketing strategies to reduce turnover by 66% and time-to-hire by 62%. Want the full Torchy’s story? Click here → Now that we’ve set the stage for what recruitment marketing is and why you need it, let’s dive into how to create a recruitment marketing strategy for your brand that’s optimized for 2025. How to Create a Recruitment Marketing Strategy That Works Phase 1: Build Your Foundation To kick off your new recruitment marketing strategy, start by defining your Employer Value Proposition (EVP). Your EVP answers the key question that we discussed at the beginning of this article – "Why should someone work for you instead of the restaurant down the street?" Consider the following factors when crafting an EVP that helps you stand out from the competition: Career advancement opportunities Competitive compensation and benefits Workplace culture and values Skills development and training programs Work-life balance initiatives Another key part of building your recruitment marketing foundation is performing an internal audit of current recruitment marketing efforts. Remember, the goal is to work smarter, not harder. Chances are, your brand is already doing some things that are working well. The point here is not to fully overhaul everything about your recruitment marketing strategy (unless absolutely necessary). It’s to build on what you’re already doing, and optimize those tactics to maximize budget and effectiveness. Review your job posting performance across platforms Analyze your careers page and application process Survey recent hires about their candidate experience Benchmark your recruitment marketing investment against industry standards Make sure to note down current recruitment metrics (cost per application, cost per hire, time to hire, interview to hire ratio, applicant to interview ratio, etc.) to track your progress once your recruitment marketing strategy is in place. Phase 2: Optimize Your Job Posting Strategy Your audit revealed which job boards deliver results—now it's time to build on what works and let go of what doesn't. Instead of playing whack-a-mole with individual job boards, use your baseline metrics to deploy integrated job posting strategies that work smarter, not harder: Set Strategic Budget Allocation : Rather than spreading your budget thin across every platform, focus your spend on the job boards and social channels that historically deliver quality candidates. For example, you could start by allocating 70% of your budget to proven performers and 30% to testing new channels. Track Performance by Platform : Monitor key metrics for each platform—applications received, quality of candidates, cost per application, and time-to-hire. This data will guide your future budget decisions. Prioritize Based on Role Urgency : Not all positions are created equal. Kitchen managers and head chefs might warrant premium job postings and social media promotion, while entry-level roles can rely on organic reach and employee referrals. Optimize Posting Timing and Frequency : Test different posting times and refresh job ads regularly. Pro Tip: Consider tools that integrate with your existing ATS to streamline reporting and cut down on busywork. This way, you’ll get a 360 view of which job boards succeed at drawing in successful candidates. Phase 3: Create a Content and Channel Strategy In 2025, the world is online. More specifically, the world is on social media. While job boards may be able to attract active job seekers to your job, remember that a significant amount of top hospitality talent are passive job seekers. Grabbing the attention of these passive job seekers requires meeting them where they are spending their time. And while they may not actively be looking on job boards, chances are that they’re still scrolling through Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, and X. With your EVP and baseline metrics, you’ll 1) create a content strategy that showcases your restaurant's unique culture, and 2) explore distribution channels to maximize reach. Consider the following ideas to create high-energy, attention-grabbing content that helps your brand stand out as a hospitality employer of choice: Employee spotlight videos and testimonials Behind-the-scenes content showing daily operations Career progression stories Day-in-the-life content for different roles Community involvement and company values demonstrations You’ll want to mix up different forms of content – videos, single images, carousels, text-based posts. Different formats work better on different platforms; this ensures that your content stays fresh and relevant to each audience. Taking Your Recruitment Marketing Strategy to the Next Level While you can manage your new recruitment marketing approach manually with spreadsheets and calendar reminders, many growing restaurant groups find that the complexity quickly becomes overwhelming. The math is simple: if you're posting across 10+ platforms for multiple roles, that's hundreds of individual posts to manage, track, and optimize each month. Add content creation, performance tracking, and budget optimization, and you're looking at a full-time job just managing your hiring marketing. Meet LANDED Plus If you’re ready to take recruitment marketing off your GMs’ and recruiting teams’ plates, our team is here to help. LANDED Plus takes the guesswork out of job board spending with proactive sponsorship management—optimizing every dollar so you get more qualified applicants, faster, while saving money. We integrate with all major ATS systems, giving you clean, streamlined reporting. And our social media team creates engaging content—like employee spotlights and behind-the-scenes videos—so your employer brand stays active without extra work for your staff. Ready to level up your recruitment marketing? Click here to chat with our team about LANDED Plus today. ‍

title: Comparing the Top 5 Commercial Fuel Cards for Fleets
summary: Compare 5 commercial fuel cards on discounts, fees, and truck stop access. AtoB's FuelMap finds cheaper diesel along your route. See the full breakdown.
body_text: Fuel is one of the highest day-to-day costs for fleet businesses, which is why many operators rely on commercial fuel cards to improve spending visibility, control driver purchases, and reduce fuel costs. Unlike standard business credit cards or business charge cards, fleet cards are designed specifically for vehicle operations, helping businesses track purchases, control driver spending, and access fuel discounts in one place. This guide compares five leading fuel card providers and explains how to evaluate the right card program based on your fleet's specific needs . Commercial Fuel Cards Aren't All the Same Not all commercial fuel cards deliver the same value. Three main fuel card types exist: Open-loop cards — Accepted anywhere Mastercard or Visa is accepted, including truck stops and retail fuel locations nationwide Proprietary network cards — Restricted to participating fuel stations within a specific network Branded cards — Limited to one fuel brand or station chain The best fleet fuel card depends on how your drivers purchase fuel, whether your fleet requires broad acceptance, and how much fuel is spent each month. Commercial Fleet Fuel Card vs. Consumer Fuel Card ‍ Feature Commercial Fleet Card Consumer Fuel Card Purchase Controls Driver PINs, gallon limits, merchant restrictions Limited controls Reporting Automated International Fuel Tax Agreement (IFTA), per-vehicle tracking Standard monthly billing statement Discounts Per-gallon fuel discounts and fleet pricing programs. Flat cash back percentages Fraud Prevention Telematics validation, card lock/unlock Basic dispute resolution ‍ Even the best credit cards for fuel , including many gas only credit cards , lack the driver-level controls and fleet management integration found in commercial solutions. Any operation with company vehicles benefits from the visibility that business fuel cards provide. What to Look for in a Fleet Fuel Card Program for Businesses Before comparing commercial fuel card providers, businesses should assess whether the program supports fuel savings, operational visibility, and spending controls. Network Coverage and Acceptance Open-loop cards backed by Mastercard or Visa offer the broadest flexibility, as they can be used at most truck stops and retail fuel stations nationwide. Broad acceptance reduces routing limitations and helps fleets avoid unnecessary out-of-network fees. This is especially important for fleets operating across multiple regions or fueling with both gas and diesel vehicles. Spend Controls and Fraud Prevention Strong controls help fleet managers monitor and control employee spending before costs escalate. Look for: Dollar transaction limits Fuel-only restrictions Time-of-day controls Real-time alerts for suspicious activity Advanced systems also validate vehicle location and fuel tank capacity before approving a fuel purchase. Reporting, Fees, and Credit Requirements The best fuel card programs simplify reporting while reducing hidden costs. Evaluate: Monthly or annual fees Per-transaction charges Automated reporting tools Accounting and billing integrations Approval requirements and underwriting structures vary by provider, particularly for newer businesses or fleets with limited operating history. Top 5 Commercial Fuel Cards Each card below serves different fleet profiles based on acceptance, discounts, and control features. 1. AtoB AtoB fuel cards are accepted anywhere Mastercard is accepted and include transparent pricing for fleet operations. The AtoB Discount Network delivers average savings of 42¢ off per gallon* on diesel at participating truck stops, plus per-gallon savings at over 30,000 locations. AtoB offers two card options: AtoB Flex — Credit with Experian reporting AtoB Unlimited — Prepaid fleet payment option designed for flexible fleet spending AtoB combines fuel savings, spend controls, reporting, and fleet expense management within a unified fleet financial platform. Both cards also include telematics-based fraud prevention with real-time GPS validation. Best for: Over the road (OTR) fleets, mixed fleets, owner-operators, and growing businesses. 2. WEX Fleet Card The WEX fuel card provides access to the WEX Nationwide Savings Network. Savings structures vary based on monthly fuel volume and network usage. Out-of-network transactions may reduce savings. Driver PINs and time-of-day restrictions provide basic controls. 3. Fuelman (FleetCor) Fuelman provides fuel management tools and rebate programs through participating fuel networks, with savings that vary based on network participation, fuel volume, and billing structure. The platform also supports fuel and maintenance purchases through its mixed fleet card program, although account and per-card fees may increase operating costs for smaller fleets. 4. Shell Fleet Navigator The Shell fleet card provides access to Shell locations plus an extended partner network. Volume-tiered rebates reward higher monthly purchases. No setup or monthly fees apply to the base card. Businesses should review current pricing, fee structures, and rebate requirements directly through Shell before applying. 5. Coast Fleet Card Coast accepts payment at any Visa location with per-gallon savings at partner stations, plus cash back on non-fuel purchases and support on expense categories beyond fuel purchases. Per-card monthly fees apply with no setup costs. Coast supports expense categories beyond fuel. OTR vs. Regional Fleet Considerations Fleet type determines which features matter most. Consider these profiles when comparing regional vs. OTR needs : ‍ Fleet Type Priority Features OTR fleets Deep truck stop discounts and automated IFTA fuel tax reporting , especially given that IFTA licensees must file quarterly IFTA fuel tax returns 1 with their base jurisdiction Regional and local fleets Universal acceptance at retail locations Mixed fleets Single card accepted everywhere without out-of-network fees Owner-operators Flexible payment structures and credit-building features. Selecting the right solution depends on where and how often your drivers fuel. How to Pick the Best Commercial Fleet Fuel Card Follow these steps to evaluate your options when selecting the right fleet fuel card program for your operation: Identify where drivers most frequently purchase fuel. Estimate your monthly fuel volume and the per-gallon savings potential. Compare total fees against projected discounts. Assess fraud exposure and implement strategies to prevent fuel card fraud using telematics-based validation. Evaluate reporting needs including IFTA automation and accounting integrations. Consider whether the card scales with tools for comprehensive fleet expense management or business banking. A fleet card can save businesses significant money over time, but only if the network and controls align with actual operating patterns. What Modern Fleet Fuel Card Platforms Provide Modern platforms extend beyond simple fuel discounts. Many now provide: Fleet management dashboards Automated reporting Fuel tracking and analytics Business banking integrations Fraud prevention tools These capabilities help fleet operators improve fleet efficiency, reduce administrative burden, and make better business decisions. AtoB combines fuel savings, controls, and reporting into one platform designed specifically for transportation businesses. Frequently Asked Questions What is a commercial fuel card and how is it different from a regular fuel card? A commercial fuel card provides per-gallon discounts, driver-level spending controls, and automated fleet reporting . Many programs also support driver PINs, purchase restrictions, and IFTA-ready reporting capabilities. Which commercial fuel card has the widest acceptance for professional drivers? Open-loop cards on the Mastercard or Visa network offer broad acceptance nationwide. Some closed-loop programs may include out-of-network restrictions or additional fees depending on where drivers purchase fuel. Can a small business fleet qualify for fuel card discounts? Fuel discounts and rebate structures vary by provider, fleet size, fuel volume, and network participation requirements. Some programs provide stronger discounts at higher monthly fuel volume levels. How do commercial fuel card discounts work at truck stops? Many commercial fuel card providers negotiate fuel pricing agreements with participating truck stop networks. Eligible discounts are typically applied automatically at participating fueling locations. What fraud protection do commercial fuel cards offer? Standard controls may include driver PINs, spending limits, merchant restrictions, and transaction alerts. Advanced platforms can also leverage the benefits of fleet telematics data for GPS validation, fuel-level tracking, and driver-level purchase monitoring. Sources Minnesota Department of Public Safety. International Fuel Tax Agreement (IFTA) Quarterly Fuel Tax Report Packet. https://assets.dps.mn.gov/files/dvs/dvs-ifta-quarterly-return-packet-ps34400-3.pdf * Average discount of 42¢ refers to realized average savings per gallon of truck diesel across AtoB customer transactions at merchant partner truck stops during H2 2025. The up to discount of $2.00 refers to max realized savings per gallon of truck diesel across AtoB customer transactions at merchant partner truck stops during H2 2025. Average discount of 5¢ off per gallon of unleaded is an average across AtoB customer transactions at merchant partner gas stations during H2 2025. ‍

title: Intuit unveils QuickBooks Workforce, radically transforming human capital management for small- and mid-market businesses
summary: All-in-one, AI-native HCM system expands on QuickBooks Payroll Services, which serves 18 Million US workers, to deliver end-to-end workforce management.
body_text: Small- and mid-market businesses often rely on seven to 25 different tools 1 to manage their workforce, creating unnecessary complexity, manual work, and fragmented data, at an estimated cost of $120,000 spent annually on software. 2 QuickBooks Workforce directly addresses this challenge, equipping businesses with a robust HCM solution that automates, simplifies, and syncs their workforce management, including payroll , time tracking , benefits , recruiting, hiring, performance, and compliance, on a single platform. Embedded directly in QuickBooks Online, QuickBooks Online Advanced, and Intuit Enterprise Suite , QuickBooks Workforce is the only HCM solution that truly enables businesses to view and manage the entire employee lifecycle alongside their financials, providing real-time insights and a holistic, 360-degree view of their business that allows them to make smarter decisions, save time and money, and operate with greater accuracy and confidence. Because QuickBooks Workforce is on the Intuit platform, a conversational “chat” interface 3 is all it takes to transform HCM from a series of manual steps into intelligent, done-for-you workflows powered by a team of virtual AI agents. This helps businesses save time on recurring tasks with features, including the Payroll Agent, which automatically collects and validates time data, flags inconsistencies, and runs payroll on behalf of the business owner while helping ensure accuracy. Other automations help streamline multi-step processes such as promotions and offboarding , connect payroll and benefits data, and unify workforce insights in real time, delivering faster and more informed decision-making that enables businesses to scale confidently while giving employees a seamless experience, from hire to retire. “The launch of QuickBooks Workforce marks the most significant evolution of Intuit’s human capital management capabilities since QuickBooks Online debuted 25 years ago,” said David Hahn, executive vice president and general manager, Services Group, Intuit. “For the first time, businesses will be able to consolidate dozens of fragmented workforce tasks into a single, end-to-end ecosystem equipped with a team of virtual AI agents and human experts, providing done-for-you workflows that streamline multi-step processes, increase accuracy, and save time. Integrating robust HCM tools directly into Intuit’s business platform, where businesses already manage critical jobs like accounting, invoicing, bill pay , and lending, reinvents how business owners manage, pay, and retain their talent by giving them a unified view of their business, empowering them to achieve greater success.”

title: New York’s AI advertising regulation goes into effect today. Are you ready?
summary: What advertisers need to know about New York’s AI disclosure law and how Hightouch Ad Studio builds compliance into the creative workflow.
body_text: Today, New York becomes the first state in the country to require advertisers to disclose when an ad features an AI-generated synthetic performer. For brands investing in AI content creation, the legislation creates an immediate operational challenge as marketers must quickly determine which ads are covered, apply the appropriate disclosures, and ensure those rules are followed consistently before anything goes live. That's why Hightouch has invested deeply in understanding these evolving requirements and building the right controls directly into our products . While you should always consult with your legal team around your business's specific obligations, here is what we believe advertisers need to know. What is New York's synthetic performer law? Signed by Governor Kathy Hochul in December 2025 and effective June 9, 2026, New York’s Synthetic Performer Disclosure Law requires advertisements distributed to audiences in the state to conspicuously disclose when they knowingly include a “synthetic performer”, defined as “as a digital asset created, reproduced, or modified by computer using generative AI or a software algorithm, intended to give the impression of a human performer in an audio, audiovisual, or visual performance, when it is not recognizable as any identifiable natural performer.” Put simply, when an advertisement features an AI-generated person who appears to be real, it must be clearly disclosed as AI. The law applies to any company that creates or produces ads featuring AI-generated people, including companies based outside New York, if those ads are distributed in the state. One important callout here is that the law applies to advertisements distributed in New York, not only ads targeted to New York residents . That means brands can’t rely solely on excluding New York residents from their targeting audiences. Instead, they need a consistent way to apply disclosures whenever an ad featuring an AI-generated person may be shown in the state. Certain uses are exempt, including audio-only ads, AI used solely for translation, and some ads and promotional materials for expressive works like movies, TV shows, and video games featuring AI performers. Violations can result in a civil penalty of $1,000 for a first offense and $5,000 for each subsequent offense. This is bigger than New York While New York’s law focuses on ads that feature AI-generated people, it’s part of a much broader shift in how governments are approaching AI-generated content. Brands will increasingly be expected to disclose when AI was used to create content. Beginning in August 2026, the EU AI Act introduces additional transparency requirements. These include machine-readable disclosures for certain types of AI-generated content. Other governments (e.g, California) and ad platforms are also moving in the same direction. These evolving regulations create a quickly growing set of requirements across creative types, markets, & platforms, and managing all of that manually will get complicated fast. For some brands, this growing complexity may raise a larger question: Is using AI-generated creative worth it at all? We don’t believe marketers need to make that tradeoff. Compliance can and should be built directly into the creative workflow so teams can continue moving quickly with AI. How Hightouch Ad Studio builds compliance into the creative workflow Hightouch Ad Studio is designed to support compliance in two ways. (1) It applies the visible disclosures consumers see, and (2) it embeds machine-readable metadata that platforms can detect. Because requirements vary by market, Ad Studio also gives marketers direct control over when and how each type of disclosure is applied. Visible AI disclosures When Ad Studio generates an ad featuring an AI-generated person, it can automatically add a visible disclosure label to the asset. Brands can control how and where that label appears, ensuring the disclosure is applied consistently Add disclosures to creative that includes people in Hightouch. Machine-readable watermarking Ad Studio also embeds invisible, machine-readable metadata into every AI-generated creative. Platforms like Meta and Google read this signal to automatically surface native " AI info" labels in their ad environments for consumers. Meta will automatically apply an AI label if they can detect that it was made with third-party tools, which is what invisible watermarking supports. Configurable controls Disclosure needs vary by market and brand policy. Ad Studio lets teams set defaults at the brand profile level, controlling when labels and watermarks apply, whether they apply to all AI content or only on faces and likenesses, and where visible labels are positioned. Defaults can be overridden at launch. Set default rules for all of your AI-generated creative. Review and override when you download or launch creative. Why this matters now The pressure on paid media teams to produce more creative quickly isn't slowing down, and the regulatory landscape is only going to expand. The challenge isn’t identifying AI-generated content once. It’s ensuring disclosures are applied consistently across hundreds or thousands of creative variants. As more governments and advertising platforms introduce their own requirements, compliance needs to become a core part of every brand’s AI strategy. Hightouch Ad Studio builds those controls directly into the creative workflow. Teams can establish consistent policies, apply the appropriate disclosures, and review the finished asset before anything goes live. That means marketers can move quickly with AI without treating compliance as an afterthought. Book a demo with our solutions experts today. Teams should consult their own legal counsel regarding their specific obligations.
